method: Per rollout step s (0-based; step s is the s-th model call), contract metric rel_absmax = max|a-r|/max|r| (float64) of: y (the step's physical output (1,1,1,G,72)), y_norm (y*mul_out+add_out in float64: every variable O(1)), window (the physical (1,2,G,84) window step s sees) and window_norm. The references are anemoi-inference rollouts of the original model (reference/run_rollout.py, identical input and forcings): cpu-fp32-pyg (ground truth), cuda-fp32-triton (runner precision '32'), cuda-fp16-triton (runner precision from the checkpoint: fp16 autocast, production). Error grows with the step, so tolerances are per step, with the one-step method of bench/calibrate_tolerances.py: fast-fp32-vs-cpu = max(1e-5, 3 x ref cuda-fp32 vs cpu) (window at step 0 = the input: 1e-6); fast-fp16-vs-cpu = 1.75 x ref cuda-fp16 vs cpu; fast-fp16-vs-ref-fp16 = 2 x ref cuda-fp16 vs ref cuda-fp32 (two independent roundings add); floors 1e-6; rounded up to 2 significant digits. v2 (fp16 keys; v1 kept under 'v1'): one fp16 reference trajectory is not a noise floor for a chaotic rollout (its error vs CPU fluctuates by ~2x from step to step and between equally valid runs). The fp16 tolerances are calibrated on an ensemble of mathematically neutral perturbations of the reference fp16 rollout (listed under 'fp16_ensemble': ANEMOI_INFERENCE_NUM_CHUNKS_* summation grouping, the pyg attention backend, 1-ulp random-sign perturbations of the input): fast-fp16-vs-cpu = 1.75 x max over {reference fp16} + ensemble of rel vs cpu (per step, per key); fast-fp16-vs-ref-fp16 = max(v1 value, 1.75 x max over the ensemble of rel vs the reference fp16 rollout), step 0 kept at the v1 one-step value. A per-step max over a handful of chaotic trajectories is heavy-tailed: valid reference runs exceed the 1.75x envelope of the OTHER runs by up to fp16_leave_one_out's worst ratio, so steps >= 1 allow that factor (fp16_allowance), and the mean over steps (a stable statistic) must stay within 1.75 x the members' largest mean (fp16_mean_tolerance). See fp16_criterion and docs/rollout.md §5.
fp16_criterion: fp16 checks (v2): step 0: rel <= the per-step tolerance (= the v1 one-step value); steps >= 1: rel <= fp16_allowance x the per-step tolerance; and per key, the mean over steps of rel <= fp16_mean_tolerance. Entries above the per-step tolerance alone are reported (valid runs have them too, see fp16_leave_one_out).
